sites.name: Do Temple (Ly Bat De Temple)
sites.event: The place of worship for the 8 kings of the Ly Dynasty, known as the birthplace of the Ly Dynasty.

sites.name: Phat Tich Pagoda (Van Phuc Tu)
sites.event: An ancient pagoda dating back to the Ly Dynasty, home to a thousand-year-old blue stone Amitabha Buddha statue (National Treasure).

sites.name: Dau Pagoda (Dien Ung Tu)
sites.event: Considered the oldest Buddhist pagoda in Vietnam, the center of the ancestral home of Vietnamese Zen Buddhism.

sites.name: But Thap Pagoda (Ninh Phuc Tu)
sites.event: Famous for its 'noi cong ngoai quoc' architecture and the largest wooden thousand-eye thousand-arm Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva statue in Vietnam.

sites.name: Ba Chua Kho Temple
sites.event: The place of worship for the woman who made great contributions to managing the food granary during the Ly Dynasty, famous for the custom of 'borrowing capital' at the beginning of the year.

sites.name: Dong Ho Painting Village
sites.event: A traditional craft village famous for Dong Ho folk woodcut paintings, a national intangible cultural heritage.

sites.name: Dinh Bang Communal House
sites.event: One of the largest and most beautiful surviving wooden communal houses in Vietnam, famous for the folk song: 'First is Dong Khang communal house, second is Dinh Bang communal house...'.

sites.name: Kinh Duong Vuong Mausoleum and Temple
sites.event: The place of worship for the Ancestor of the Vietnamese nation (Kinh Duong Vuong), father of Lac Long Quan.

sites.name: Phu Lang Pottery Village
sites.event: A traditional ancient pottery village dating back to the Tran Dynasty, famous for its eel-skin glazed ceramics.

sites.name: Bac Ninh Temple of Literature
sites.event: The place of worship for Confucius and honoring the sages and scholars of the ancient Kinh Bac region.

sites.name: Luy Lau Ancient Citadel
sites.event: Once the largest political, economic, cultural, and Buddhist center of Giao Chi during the period of Northern domination.
